_about.what: Carriers and the air war at sea (the grand campaign only). A carrier is a floating airfield: every fleet with carriers has a wing of fighters and a wing of strike aircraft that go where the fleet goes. They are air groups like any other, planned from the same raid planner, and they are counted in the same Battle Ticket. None of this touches the history campaigns.
_about.wing: The aircraft one carrier brings, by navy: fighters and strike aircraft (bombers). A fleet's two wings are kept at that many for each carrier it has. names gives the wings their names: {fleet} is the fleet they sail with.
_about.range: How far carrier aircraft reach, in kilometres. A fleet at sea reaches every coast of the sea it is in at no distance, and ground inland as far from that coast as the range allows. 'next' is what a neighbouring sea counts as: bombers reach it, fighters cover it at part effect. A fleet in harbour flies from its port like any airfield. quality is what carrier aircraft are worth beside the same navy's land fighters.
_about.naval: What one bomber is worth against ships. Carrier crews are trained for it ('carrier'); land bombers mostly are not ('land', by nation).
_about.strike: A strike on one fleet at sea, which stands for a month of sorties. Hits = bombers that get through x their worth against ships x hit, less what the fighter cover spoils (spoil x the square root of the defending fighters' share of the fight, so even a few fighters break up a good deal of an unescorted strike). The hits fall on the classes by 'aim' x how many there are, and a ship of a class takes 'takes' hits to sink. No strike sinks more than 'most' of a fleet's surface ships; a second strike on the same fleet in a month finds it scattered and warned ('again' for each strike before it). A fleet at sea known only from a report is harder to find: 'report' of the strike arrives (a harbour does not move, and is struck in full). 'ready' is the fitness for sea the fleet loses when every ship is hit, and 'value' is what a ship of each class counts for when the raid is judged, in aircraft. 'dc' is ruling 240's Damage control (behind the switch research.dc, off as shipped): a fleet whose nation holds it takes 'dc' times the hits to sink, its surface warships only. The class totals and the cap ('most') are worked first, on the count without anyone's damage control, and only then is each fleet's own share divided by its own 'dc': so a navy's losses never hang on the research of another lying beside it, and the hits are not changed. Wherever else a surface warship is sunk the same 'dc' divides the chance: navy.json's 'tough' for its class in a fleet action, under the land bombers' monthly toll, from shore batteries answering a bombardment and in the older air strike, and the chance that a submarine's torpedo sinks the ship it has hit. Submarines, the destroyers lost hunting them, convoy escorts and merchant tonnage are never touched.
_about.harbour: A raid on ships lying in harbour. They cannot manoeuvre: hits are multiplied by 'hit', and up to 'most' can be sunk. In the month war is declared the harbour is caught unready: its fighters and guns count 'unready' and the hits are multiplied by 'surprise'.
_about.flak: Ships' anti-aircraft guns. The share of the bombers they bring down is per x the guns of the ships under attack (by class), never more than 'most'. Ruling 240, behind the switches in 'research' (off as shipped; with them off the two numbers that follow are never read): each fleet's guns count 'stage' times their weight by its nation's research (early, mid or late; mid is the weight the guns always had), and 'vt' times that again where it has proximity shells. The cap goes by weight of guns: what the plain weight would bring down, never more than 'most', in the share the staged weight is of the plain weight. So a fleet at 1.5 can reach 1.5 x 'most', and in a harbour no navy lifts the cap for another lying beside it. Guns on land are not changed.
_about.cap: Fighter cover. 'spoil' is how much of a strike a strong fighter cover breaks up. Carrier fighters with a fleet also keep the enemy's coastal bombers off it: the monthly toll those take is cut by fighters / (fighters + scale), by no more than 'most'.
_about.sunk: When a carrier is sunk the aircraft aboard go with it, but 'saved' of them land on another deck or ashore.
_about.empty: What a carrier with no aircraft is still worth in a fleet action, with a convoy or hunting submarines, beside one with its full wings.
_about.search: Finding ships at sea. A nation's search of a sea is the ships its side has there (by class; carriers count by their aircraft), its carriers in neighbouring seas ('next' each), 'air' for each point of its coastal air strength over that sea, and 'flight' where its aircraft have searched the sea this month. A fleet is identified at 'find' and reported (ships are there, not what) at 'report'; open ocean needs more (x 1 + open x (1 - how well the coasts' aircraft cover that sea)), and submarines alone need 'subs' times as much. A fleet that fights, shells a coast or strikes with its aircraft is identified by its enemy that month and reported the month after. Ships in harbour are always reported, and identified where the port is in full view; a nation at peace with you hides nothing in its harbours.
_about.ai: The computer's admirals and air staff. A carrier wing strikes the best fleet its side has found in reach, or ships in a harbour, where the forecast gives 'success' or better and the wing's losses stay under 'loss'; its fighters go with the bombers when fighters will come up. 'landShare' of a nation's land bomber groups fit to fly may also be sent against ships, and only against a fleet that is identified. A carrier fleet in harbour puts to sea to strike where its side would be 'sortie' times the enemy there. A fleet struck from the air keeps out of that sea for 'shy' months, unless the homeland is invaded across it. Ruling 52: with 'trade', a computer staff weighs a strike at the enemy's cargoes beside his warships (a sea his convoys cross, or where his coasters run under his own shore), within the same 'landShare'; and it flies up to 'searches' searches of the sea a month, as a player's are flown and at the same cost, where enemy ships are reported and not identified, where its side was attacked at sea since last month, and off its own harbours and stations in turn.
_about.research: Ruling 240 (Brian, 21 November 2026: 'yes to all 3'; release 2). Three rules for ships that read research alone: never a nation, a date, which side attacks or who the player is. Each has its own switch, read every time it is asked, and ALL THREE ARE OFF as shipped: with a switch off its rule changes nothing, and its research row (tech.json, a row marked 'ships' with the switch's name) is shelved, so nobody researches it and no card shows it. 'stage': a fleet's anti-aircraft guns are late-war where its nation holds the technology named in 'late', mid-war where it holds the one in 'mid', otherwise early-war (flak.stage). 'vt': proximity shells, the technology in 'tech' (flak.vt). 'dc': damage control, the technology in 'tech' (strike.dc). The fleet of a kin nation (arsenal.json plans.kin) takes the better of its own and its senior partner's. The grand campaign only: a history campaign has no research tree, and nothing here reaches it whatever the switches say.

_wingByDate: A carrier's wing by navy and by date (release 2, the switch 'Carrier wings by date', stage.json wingByDate; the design director's riders of 17 November 2026, 12:01Z and 12:12Z, to rulings 189 and 202; the historian's british-carrier-wing-check.md). Rows of [from month, fighters, strike aircraft] a deck, each read from its month on; before the first row the navy's own 'wing' stands. Britain's is the one dated navy: 12 and 24 from September 1939, 24 and 12 from August 1942 (month 36), 28 and 20 from January 1944 (53), 37 and 17 from January 1945 (65). Where a step lowers a kind, what is over goes to the reserve; where it raises one, the room fills as losses are made good, in harbour, from the reserve: nothing is given (carriers.ts syncWings). Every stop of the dial and every British carrier, Europe's too. 'words': the UI director's line for a player who is Britain (passed 16 November, 12:16Z), an ordinary news line shown only while he has a carrier afloat or building. Apart from the switch, a fleet whose row gives 'deck' below one (ruling 189(b): a light carrier that sailed alone) brings that share of its navy's wing a carrier.

UK.words: The Fleet Air Arm re-equips: each of your carriers now has deck room for {ftr} fighters and {bmr} strike aircraft, where it had room for {wasFtr} and {wasBmr}.
